problem_statement: Rebrand and restyle the Revolve Bulma personal-magazine demo into a fresh, coherent fictional publication called Saltmarsh & Signal, a coastal field journal about lighthouse-keeping, tidal navigation, and shoreline craft edited by relief keeper Marina Holloway. Rework the homepage slider, homepage post grid, the category page, and the about page so their headlines, captions, categories, image alt text, newsletter block, footer wordmark, and page titles all read as one editorial voice, while keeping the Revolve template structure, Bulma layout, navigation, and responsive behaviour intact. The demo copy (travel/food/lifestyle filler and Lorem-style demo body text) must be fully replaced across these surfaces, not just on the homepage hero.
required_content: Rebrand the homepage slider hero into Saltmarsh & Signal coastal stories with real headlines (for example Trimming the Wick for a Long Winter Watch) and descriptive image alt text.

Replace the homepage post grid with a coherent editorial-image system: a From the Coast intro heading, coastal field-note cards with consistent crops and descriptive captions, and meaningful alt text on every image.
Rework the category page (fashion.html) so its breadcrumb, cards, and captions read as the Tidework section of Saltmarsh & Signal rather than the demo travel/food filler.
Rewrite the about page so it introduces keeper Marina Holloway and the purpose of the journal instead of the demo Lorem-style biography.
Rebrand shared chrome: the browser title, logo alt text, newsletter block, and footer wordmark, so no visible Revolve or demo-filler text remains on the reworked surfaces.

Add a shared Coast Signal tide rail that appears on the homepage, the Tidework category page, and the About page, carrying a Coast Signal kicker, a 'Today on the Saltmarsh & Signal watch' heading, and four coastal status tiles (working tide, lamp state, wind, next relief watch).
Wire the Coast Signal section filter so clicking the Tidework chip updates the live readout to 'Now showing: Tidework — creeks, channels and crossings', keeping the highlight and readout in sync.

Keep the Coast Signal tile row responsive so it wraps without horizontal overflow on mobile, and keep the rail palette on-brand with the cream/terracotta editorial voice rather than an off-theme dark panel.
design_constraints: Keep the Revolve editorial style and Bulma column layout: cream header, serif headlines, small uppercase category labels, muted dates, clean white spacing, and the existing navigation, slider, newsletter, and footer structure.
The rebrand should read as one native editorial voice, not a generic card redesign, ecommerce grid, dashboard, or marketing section.
Use the existing local images in source/images only; do not introduce external stock photos, generated images, icon packs, or raster mockups.
Image crops should preserve subjects and avoid stretched, distorted, or mismatched framing across desktop, tablet, and mobile.
Mobile must keep images, titles, dates, menu, newsletter, and footer readable without horizontal overflow or overlapping captions.

The Coast Signal rail must read as part of the Saltmarsh & Signal editorial system on every page it appears, and its filter must keep the highlighted chip and the readout text consistent after interaction.
state_constraints: The homepage at /index.html must remain the main reference surface and should still show the slider, post grid, pagination, newsletter, and footer.
The category page at /fashion.html and the about page at /about.html are regression and cross-page surfaces that must be rebranded to the same Saltmarsh & Signal editorial voice as the homepage.

change_completion: All reworked surfaces (slider, post grid, category page, about page) carry the Saltmarsh & Signal coastal editorial voice with real headlines and captions.
The shared Coast Signal tide rail appears on the homepage, the Tidework category page, and the About page, with the Coast Signal kicker, watch heading, four status tiles, and section filter.
design_consistency: Headlines, category labels, captions, alt text, newsletter, and footer wordmark read as one coherent publication across pages.
The Coast Signal rail keeps the on-brand cream/terracotta Unna-serif palette rather than an off-theme dark or grey panel, matching the reference rail visually.
responsive: The homepage, category, and about pages stay readable on desktop, tablet, and mobile viewports with no horizontal overflow.
On mobile the Coast Signal tile row wraps to full width instead of forcing a fixed nowrap row that overflows the small screen.
regression: The existing Revolve/Bulma template layout, navigation, slider behaviour, newsletter, footer, and internal links remain intact and are not broken or removed.
The Coast Signal section filter keeps the highlighted chip and the readout text in sync after interaction, so the existing behaviour still works.
